cards.title: Introduction to Databases in Python
cards.content: Python applications frequently need to store, retrieve, and manipulate persistent data. We achieve this using databases, which fall primarily into two categories: Relational (SQL) and Non-Relational (NoSQL).

options.text: PostgreSQL is a NoSQL document store.
SQLite is a lightweight, file-based relational database.
MongoDB requires a predefined rigid schema for all collections.

cards.title: Using SQLite with Python
cards.content:
Python comes with a built-in library for SQLite called sqlite3. No external installation is required.

import sqlite3

conn = sqlite3.connect('my_database.db')
cursor = conn.cursor()

cursor.execute('''
    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        name TEXT NOT NULL
    )
''')
conn.commit()
conn.close()

content.text: To connect to an SQLite database file named 'app.db', you import sqlite3 and call sqlite3._____('app.db').

cards.title: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM)
cards.content: Writing raw SQL queries can become cumbersome. An ORM allows you to interact with your database using Python classes and objects instead of writing raw SQL strings. Popular Python ORMs include SQLAlchemy and Django ORM.

Handles the dialog with the database (add, commit, rollback).
Maps Python classes to database tables.

cards.title: Working with NoSQL (MongoDB)
cards.content:
For unstructured or rapidly changing data, document databases like MongoDB are ideal. In Python, we use the pymongo library to interact with MongoDB.

from pymongo import MongoClient

client = MongoClient('mongodb://localhost:27017/')
db = client['my_database']
collection = db['users']

collection.insert_one({'name': 'Alice', 'role': 'Developer'})

cards.title: Database Migrations with Alembic
cards.content: When your database schema evolves over time (e.g., adding a new column), you use migrations. In the SQLAlchemy ecosystem, Alembic is the standard tool used to manage and version schema changes.

cards.title: Summary
cards.content: You now understand the basics of connecting Python to SQLite, structuring queries, utilizing ORMs like SQLAlchemy, working with NoSQL via PyMongo, and managing migrations!
